healthcareSystem: Mixed public-private system. Public hospitals are under-resourced. Private clinics in Douala and Yaoundé offer better quality. Bilingual country (French and English) though French dominates healthcare. Quality drops significantly outside major cities.
qualityNotes: Private hospitals in Douala and Yaoundé provide reasonable care for common conditions. Public hospitals can be overcrowded and poorly equipped. English-speaking healthcare available in the anglophone regions (Northwest and Southwest). For serious conditions, evacuation to South Africa or Europe may be needed.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in cities open 8am-7pm weekdays. Some pharmacies de garde (duty pharmacies) operate at night and weekends. Limited availability in rural areas.
pharmacyTips: Buy only from licensed pharmacies with the green cross sign. Street-sold medications are widespread but often counterfeit or expired. Pharmacists in Douala and Yaoundé speak French and sometimes English. Bring essential medications from home.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is lax. Many medications including antibiotics available without prescription at pharmacies. Quality assurance is a concern — buy only from licensed pharmacies.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly illegal. Severe penalties including imprisonment.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry documentation. Opioid-based medications require a doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry original packaging and prescription documentation in French or English.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names. French or English documentation accepted (bilingual preferred). Keep medications in original packaging. Bring sufficient supply for your trip.

travelInsurance.tips: Medical evacuation coverage is essential. Serious conditions require evacuation to South Africa or Europe. Ensure malaria treatment is covered. Check security exclusions — some regions have travel advisories.

recommended: Malaria prophylaxis (essential — malaria is endemic throughout Cameroon)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow Fever vaccination is REQUIRED for all travelers. Malaria prophylaxis is essential year-round and throughout the country. Northern Cameroon is in the meningitis belt.

waterNotes: Tap water is NOT safe to drink anywhere in Cameroon. Use only bottled or thoroughly purified water for drinking and brushing teeth. Avoid ice in drinks outside international hotels. Bottled water (Tangui brand) is widely available.
foodSafetyTips: Eat at established restaurants. Avoid raw vegetables and unpeeled fruits. Street food from busy vendors (grilled fish, soya/suya) is generally safer when freshly cooked. Ndolé and other traditional dishes are usually well-cooked. Wash hands frequently.
medicalTourismNote: Cameroon is not a medical tourism destination. Private hospitals in Douala serve the regional community.
metaDescription: Health guide for Cameroon: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, bottled water only, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Centre Hospitalier d'Essos (CHE)
hospitals.notes: Well-regarded hospital in the capital. French-speaking. Decent facilities by local standards.

hospitals.name: Clinique de la Cathédrale
hospitals.notes: Private clinic in Douala. Good reputation. French-speaking with some English.

hospitals.name: Hôpital Général de Douala
hospitals.notes: Major public hospital in Douala. Good emergency department. Primarily French-speaking.

hospitals.name: Bamenda Regional Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital in the English-speaking Northwest Region. English-speaking staff. Basic but accessible for tourists in the Ring Road area.

dentalCare.availability: Available in Douala and Yaoundé at private clinics. Limited elsewhere.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care quality is variable. Private dental clinics in Douala are the best option. Sterilization standards may not meet international norms at all facilities.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, seek a private clinic in Douala or Yaoundé. Ask your hotel or embassy for recommendations.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated mental health crisis line available
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. Some English-speaking counselors in Bamenda and Buea.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are very limited. French-speaking psychiatric services available at university hospitals. English-speaking support is scarce. Telehealth from your home country recommended.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited throughout Cameroon.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major hospitals in Douala and Yaoundé have basic wheelchair access. Smaller facilities do not.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Private vehicles are the main option.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Roads can be in poor condition, especially outside major cities. Bring all assistive devices. Contact accommodations in advance about accessibility needs.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at major hospitals in Douala and Yaoundé.
covidStatus.notes: COVID restrictions have been fully lifted. Standard precautions recommended.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private clinics can provide receipts in French. Pay cash and submit for reimbursement. Have documents translated if needed. Keep all receipts and medical records. Contact your insurer before major treatment.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs. Payment in Central African CFA franc (XAF). Private clinics are more expensive but offer better care.

medicalEvacuation.primaryDestination: Johannesburg, South Africa or Paris, France
medicalEvacuation.secondaryDestination: Douala to Yaoundé (domestic), or Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire
medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation is necessary for serious conditions. Douala has the main international airport for evacuations. Ensure your insurance covers evacuation to South Africa or Europe.
